title: Effect of bradykinin-receptor blockade on the response to angiotensin-converting-enzyme inhibitor in normotensive and hypertensive subjects
authors: Gainer JV, Morrow JD, Loveland A, King DJ, Brown NJ
population: 20 normotensive and 7 hypertensive subjects, salt depleted on 10 mmol sodium per day
funder: not read: the publisher page is not accessible and the PubMed abstract carries no funding statement. PubMed lists NIH grants GM07569, HL56963 and RR00095.
result: Single-blind randomised crossover of captopril 25 mg, captopril with the bradykinin B2 receptor antagonist icatibant (100 µg/kg), losartan 75 mg and placebo. Icatibant attenuated the maximal fall in mean arterial pressure with captopril from 14.0 to 10.5 mm Hg (P=0.001), to a value similar to losartan (11.0 mm Hg), and altered the change in plasma renin activity with captopril (-0.4 against +2.0 ng angiotensin I/ml/h with captopril alone, P=0.007), without altering the renal haemodynamic response; effects were similar in normotensive and hypertensive and in Black and white subjects. The authors conclude that bradykinin contributes to the short-term blood-pressure effect of ACE inhibition.
